title: Fever-like temperatures improve cognitive deficits in the Scn2a autism mouse model via increases in potassium channel activity.
abstract: In some children with autism, fever improves cognition. Using the Scn2a autism mouse model, fever-like temperatures independent of direct immune activation normalized cognitive function. Scn2a juvenile mice at normal body temperature failed to learn an escape route, whereas Scn2a mice exposed to infrared light-induced fever exhibited normal learning. In somatosensory cortex, fever-like temperatures reduced excess spiking in Scn2a pyramidal neurons by increasing potassium channel activation and spike threshold. Chemogenetically reducing spiking at normal temperatures replicated the effects of fever.
